scope: Orthodox chess with policy notes for Chess960-aware castling handling.

invariants.name: side_to_move_defined
invariants.assertion: state.turn is either white or black.
invariants.why: Active color is part of the state and repetition identity.

invariants.name: color_occupancies_disjoint
invariants.assertion: white_occupancy & black_occupancy == 0.
invariants.why: No square can hold both colors.

invariants.name: occupancy_union_matches_total
invariants.assertion: all_occupancy == (white_occupancy | black_occupancy).
invariants.why: Internal occupancy masks must agree.

invariants.name: piece_type_bitboards_disjoint
invariants.assertion: No square appears in more than one piece-type set.
invariants.why: A square cannot simultaneously contain multiple piece types.

invariants.name: board_array_matches_bitboards
invariants.assertion: Mailbox/array view and bitboards encode the same board.
invariants.why: Mixed representations drift easily after make/unmake bugs.

invariants.name: piece_lists_match_board
invariants.assertion: Piece lists and piece-count tables match square contents exactly.
invariants.why: Piece-list corruption is a classic move/unmove failure mode.

invariants.name: square_uniqueness
invariants.assertion: Each occupied square contains exactly one piece record.
invariants.why: Duplicate square ownership indicates structural corruption.

invariants.name: exactly_one_white_king
invariants.assertion: There is exactly one white king on the board.
invariants.why: Standard chess requires one king per side.

invariants.name: exactly_one_black_king
invariants.assertion: There is exactly one black king on the board.
invariants.why: Standard chess requires one king per side.

invariants.name: white_piece_budget
invariants.assertion: White has at most 16 men.
invariants.why: A side cannot retain more than its original sixteen men.

invariants.name: black_piece_budget
invariants.assertion: Black has at most 16 men.
invariants.why: A side cannot retain more than its original sixteen men.

invariants.name: white_pawn_budget
invariants.assertion: White has at most 8 pawns.
invariants.why: A side starts with eight pawns and promotions remove pawns.

invariants.name: black_pawn_budget
invariants.assertion: Black has at most 8 pawns.
invariants.why: A side starts with eight pawns and promotions remove pawns.

invariants.name: total_piece_budget
invariants.assertion: Total occupied squares with pieces is at most 32.
invariants.why: Orthodox chess has 32 physical men maximum.

invariants.name: no_pawns_on_backrank
invariants.assertion: No pawn occupies rank 1 or rank 8.
invariants.why: A pawn that reaches the back rank must promote immediately.

invariants.name: castling_rights_mask_sane
invariants.assertion: Castling-right bits are from the supported set only.
invariants.why: Corrupted rights create false legal moves and false repetition keys.

invariants.name: castling_rights_structurally_consistent
invariants.assertion: If castling rights are present, the corresponding king and rook mapping is structurally valid for the chosen variant.
invariants.why: Libraries and engines validate castling rights against board structure.
invariants.implementation_notes: In orthodox chess this usually means king on e1/e8 and rook on a/h; in Chess960 use your start-file mapping.

invariants.name: ep_square_shape_spec
invariants.assertion: Under FEN-spec mode, EP square is absent or on rank 3/6 consistent with the external notation rules.
invariants.why: The FEN spec defines EP as a target square field of the state.
invariants.implementation_notes: This is the external I/O policy, not necessarily the internal canonical form.

invariants.name: ep_square_shape_strict
invariants.assertion: Under strict-internal mode, EP square is absent or also satisfies local capture preconditions.
invariants.why: Stockfish sanitizes EP more aggressively than the original FEN spec.
invariants.implementation_notes: Recommended internal canonicalization policy if you want a tighter state invariant.

invariants.name: halfmove_clock_nonnegative
invariants.assertion: halfmove_clock >= 0.
invariants.why: The halfmove clock is a nonnegative FEN field.

invariants.name: fullmove_number_positive
invariants.assertion: fullmove_number >= 1.
invariants.why: The fullmove number in FEN starts at 1 and increments after Black's move.

invariants.name: ply_counter_consistent
invariants.assertion: If a separate ply counter is stored, it is consistent with fullmove_number and side_to_move.
invariants.why: Counter drift breaks PGN/FEN export and search bookkeeping.

invariants.name: zobrist_hash_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: Position hash equals a clean recomputation from board + turn + castling + EP.
invariants.why: TT corruption and repetition bugs often surface here first.

invariants.name: pawn_hash_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: Pawn hash equals a clean recomputation from pawn locations and any side-dependent pawn features if used.
invariants.why: Useful for engines with pawn hash tables.

invariants.name: material_key_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: Material key / material signature matches recomputation.
invariants.why: Stockfish checks material consistency in pos_is_ok().

invariants.name: attack_cache_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: Cached attack maps match recomputation from the board.
invariants.why: Invalid attack caches create false checks and false legal moves.

invariants.name: checkers_cache_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: Cached checker set equals recomputation.
invariants.why: Many engines cache 'checkers' or 'in_check' incrementally.

invariants.name: pinners_blockers_cache_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: Pinned-piece and blocker caches match a fresh computation.
invariants.why: Pinned move legality is highly sensitive to stale caches.

invariants.name: eval_cache_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: If incremental material/PSQT/eval caches exist, they match full recomputation in debug mode.
invariants.why: This catches silent evaluation drift unrelated to rule legality.

invariants.name: nnue_accumulator_matches_refresh
invariants.assertion: If NNUE or similar accumulators are incremental, a forced refresh matches the current accumulator.
invariants.why: Search correctness depends on cache coherence even when move legality is correct.
invariants.implementation_notes: Optional if the engine uses incremental neural accumulators.

invariants.name: move_stack_frame_integrity
invariants.assertion: Top undo frame is structurally complete whenever a move is pushed.
invariants.why: Unmake correctness requires exact saved state.

invariants.name: repetition_stack_length_consistent
invariants.assertion: The repetition-history stack length matches the move stack / ply count policy.
invariants.why: Repetition logic depends on a faithful key history.

invariants.name: side_not_to_move_not_in_check
invariants.assertion: In a legal resulting position, the side that just moved is not left in check.
invariants.why: FIDE legality forbids making a move that leaves your own king in check.

invariants.name: kings_not_adjacent
invariants.assertion: The two kings do not attack each other from adjacent squares.
invariants.why: Adjacent kings imply an illegal position.

invariants.name: checker_count_at_most_two
invariants.assertion: The checked side has at most two independent checking pieces.
invariants.why: In orthodox chess, more than two simultaneous checkers is impossible.

invariants.name: opposite_check_rejected
invariants.assertion: Reject states where the side not to move is in check.
invariants.why: python-chess exposes this as OPPOSITE_CHECK and Stockfish rejects king-capturable states.

invariants.name: impossible_check_patterns_rejected
invariants.assertion: Reject or warn on impossible check geometries that cannot arise from a legal last move.
invariants.why: python-chess includes IMPOSSIBLE_CHECK and TOO_MANY_CHECKERS as import-time sanity checks.

invariants.name: legal_moves_are_pseudolegal
invariants.assertion: Every move in the legal move list is also pseudo-legal under piece movement rules.
invariants.why: A legal move generator should refine, not contradict, pseudo-legal generation.

invariants.name: legal_filter_removes_self_check_only
invariants.assertion: Pseudo-legal moves become legal exactly when they do not leave the mover's king in check.
invariants.why: The difference between pseudo-legal and legal move sets should be explained by king safety.

invariants.name: no_move_captures_king
invariants.assertion: No legal move captures a king.
invariants.why: Checkmate ends the game; kings are never captured in legal chess.

invariants.name: king_move_destination_not_attacked
invariants.assertion: Every legal king move lands on a square not attacked by the opponent.
invariants.why: This is the core king-safety condition.

invariants.name: pinned_piece_moves_preserve_ray
invariants.assertion: A legal move by a pinned piece stays on the pin ray unless it captures the pinning piece in a legal way.
invariants.why: Pinned-piece handling is a common movegen bug source.

invariants.name: castling_requires_right
invariants.assertion: A castling move is legal only if the relevant historical castling right is still present.
invariants.why: Castling legality depends partly on history, not just geometry.

invariants.name: castling_path_empty
invariants.assertion: All squares between king and rook are empty for a legal castling move.
invariants.why: FIDE requires no intervening pieces.

invariants.name: castling_squares_not_attacked
invariants.assertion: For a legal castling move, the king's start, transit, and destination squares are not under attack.
invariants.why: FIDE castling rules explicitly require this.

invariants.name: castling_rook_king_destinations_correct
invariants.assertion: A castling move relocates king and rook to the correct final squares under the supported variant.
invariants.why: Move application must match the rules exactly.

invariants.name: castling_forbidden_while_in_check
invariants.assertion: Castling is not legal when the king starts the move in check.
invariants.why: FIDE explicitly forbids castling out of check.

invariants.name: en_passant_requires_last_move_history
invariants.assertion: An en passant capture is legal only on the reply immediately following the opponent's double pawn push.
invariants.why: This is a history-sensitive rule, not a geometric rule alone.

invariants.name: en_passant_target_square_correct
invariants.assertion: A pseudo-legal en passant capture targets the current EP square and the captured pawn sits on the passed square.
invariants.why: EP application bugs often remove the wrong pawn or square.

invariants.name: en_passant_preserves_king_safety
invariants.assertion: An en passant move is legal only if removing both pawns does not expose the moving side's king.
invariants.why: EP is the special move most likely to break incremental attack logic.

invariants.name: promotion_from_last_rank_transition_only
invariants.assertion: A promotion occurs only when a pawn moves from its penultimate rank to the back rank.
invariants.why: Promotion cannot happen from arbitrary squares.

invariants.name: promotion_piece_set_restricted
invariants.assertion: Promotion result is one of queen, rook, bishop, or knight.
invariants.why: FIDE restricts promotion choices to these four pieces.

invariants.name: promotion_replaces_pawn_immediately
invariants.assertion: After promotion, the pawn no longer exists on the destination square; the promoted piece does.
invariants.why: Promotion is immediate and final on that move.

invariants.name: double_pawn_push_preconditions
invariants.assertion: A two-square pawn advance starts from the home rank, crosses an empty square, and lands on an empty square.
invariants.why: Piece movement rules define this precisely.

invariants.name: pawn_move_geometry_correct
invariants.assertion: Single pushes, captures, and promotions follow pawn geometry exactly for the side to move.
invariants.why: Pawn bugs generate many downstream legality failures.

invariants.name: slider_paths_unobstructed
invariants.assertion: Bishop, rook, and queen moves traverse unobstructed rays.
invariants.why: Ray bugs create phantom moves and missed attacks.

invariants.name: knight_move_geometry_correct
invariants.assertion: Knight moves use L-shaped geometry and ignore interposing pieces.
invariants.why: Knights are the main non-ray exception.

invariants.name: king_move_geometry_correct
invariants.assertion: Non-castling king moves are one square in any direction and obey occupancy/attack rules.
invariants.why: Separates basic geometry from castling logic.

invariants.name: checkmate_definition_exact
invariants.assertion: If in check and with no legal moves, the state is checkmate.
invariants.why: Terminal classification should match the Laws of Chess exactly.

invariants.name: stalemate_definition_exact
invariants.assertion: If not in check and with no legal moves, the state is stalemate.
invariants.why: Terminal classification should match the Laws of Chess exactly.

invariants.name: dead_position_not_conflated_with_simple_material
invariants.assertion: Do not equate 'dead position' with a simplistic insufficient-material heuristic; if using a heuristic, label it as such.
invariants.why: FIDE's dead-position rule is semantic, not merely a material-count table.
invariants.implementation_notes: Use exact dead-position logic if you implement it; otherwise expose a weaker 'insufficient material heuristic' name.

invariants.name: legal_move_count_matches_recompute
invariants.assertion: A fresh legal move recomputation yields the same count and set as the incremental generator.
invariants.why: This is a strong deep-check invariant.

invariants.name: attackers_to_consistent
invariants.assertion: attackers_to(square, side) matches a fresh attack generator or inverse move generator.
invariants.why: Attack queries are used across check, SEE, pins, castling, and evaluation.

invariants.name: attacked_squares_stable_after_make_unmake
invariants.assertion: Attack maps before a move equal attack maps after make+unmake.
invariants.why: This catches incremental attack-cache drift.

invariants.name: castling_rights_monotone
invariants.assertion: Castling rights never reappear once lost.
invariants.why: Castling rights are historical entitlements, not dynamic geometric facts.

invariants.name: king_move_clears_both_rights
invariants.assertion: Moving a king clears both castling rights for that side.
invariants.why: This follows directly from the castling rule.

invariants.name: rook_home_move_clears_right
invariants.assertion: Moving a rook from its original castling square clears the corresponding castling right.
invariants.why: The relevant rook must not have moved previously.

invariants.name: rook_home_capture_clears_right
invariants.assertion: Capturing a rook on its original castling square clears that side's corresponding castling right if still present.
invariants.why: Rights can be lost by rook disappearance as well as rook movement.

invariants.name: castling_move_clears_side_rights
invariants.assertion: Executing castling clears both castling rights for the moving side.
invariants.why: After the king moves, castling is permanently lost.

invariants.name: ep_square_set_per_policy
invariants.assertion: After a legal double pawn push, set the EP square according to the chosen policy (spec-FEN or strict-captureable).
invariants.why: The specification and internal canonicalization policy may differ here.
invariants.implementation_notes: Preserve external I/O fidelity even if your internal canonical state is stricter.

invariants.name: ep_square_cleared_when_expired
invariants.assertion: EP availability disappears after one opponent reply if unused.
invariants.why: FIDE says en passant is legal only on the immediately following move.

invariants.name: ep_square_cleared_on_non_qualifying_move
invariants.assertion: Any move that is not a fresh double pawn push leaves no EP target square afterward.
invariants.why: A stale EP square creates false legal moves and wrong repetition keys.

invariants.name: halfmove_reset_on_pawn_move
invariants.assertion: Any pawn move resets the halfmove clock to zero.
invariants.why: This is defined by FEN and the move-counting rules.

invariants.name: halfmove_reset_on_capture
invariants.assertion: Any capture resets the halfmove clock to zero.
invariants.why: This is defined by FEN and the move-counting rules.

invariants.name: halfmove_increment_otherwise
invariants.assertion: A non-pawn, non-capture move increments the halfmove clock by one.
invariants.why: Halfmove maintenance drives 50/75-move logic.

invariants.name: fullmove_increment_after_black
invariants.assertion: fullmove_number increments after Black's move only.
invariants.why: This is the FEN fullmove-number convention.

invariants.name: undo_frame_is_lossless
invariants.assertion: Undo metadata stores enough information to restore board, turn, rights, EP, clocks, and hashes exactly.
invariants.why: Exact unmake is the linchpin of search correctness.

invariants.name: make_unmake_roundtrip_exact
invariants.assertion: Applying a move and then unmaking it restores the pre-move state exactly, including hashes and counters.
invariants.why: This is the most valuable transition invariant in engines.

invariants.name: rebuild_from_history_matches_state
invariants.assertion: Replaying move history from the root yields the exact current state.
invariants.why: This protects against long-range drift in incremental logic.

invariants.name: null_move_toggles_turn_and_clears_ep
invariants.assertion: If null move pruning is supported, null move flips side to move, clears EP, and updates clocks without mutating pieces or rights.
invariants.why: Null move is engine-internal but still needs invariant coverage.
invariants.implementation_notes: Only relevant if the engine implements null moves.

invariants.name: repetition_key_includes_relevant_state
invariants.assertion: Position identity for repetition includes piece placement, side to move, castling rights, and relevant EP availability.
invariants.why: FIDE treats positions as different if possible moves differ because of castling or EP.

invariants.name: repetition_history_consistent
invariants.assertion: The repetition table / key multiset matches the actual stack of visited positions.
invariants.why: Threefold/fivefold draw logic depends on exact history accounting.

invariants.name: threefold_and_fivefold_derived_from_history
invariants.assertion: Threefold-claim and fivefold-automatic draw states derive from actual repeated position keys, not from ad hoc heuristics.
invariants.why: These are history-sensitive, not purely local board properties.

invariants.name: fifty_and_seventyfive_move_rules_from_clock
invariants.assertion: 50-move claimability and 75-move automatic draw logic derive from the halfmove clock and applicable exceptions.
invariants.why: These rules are defined at the game-state level.

invariants.name: fen_roundtrip_exact_under_io_policy
invariants.assertion: serialize_fen(parse_fen(fen)) preserves the intended external FEN policy or normalizes only as documented.
invariants.why: Roundtrip correctness matters for external interfaces and debugging.

invariants.name: pgn_san_roundtrip_when_supported
invariants.assertion: If SAN/PGN is implemented, parsing emitted SAN from the same state reproduces the original move.
invariants.why: Notation code is another high-value surface for rule bugs.

invariants.name: root_state_preserved_across_search
invariants.assertion: Search must not mutate the root position after completion, including clocks, stack, and hash.
invariants.why: Search bugs can leak mutations via TT, PV, or null-move paths.

invariants.name: principal_variation_replay_legal
invariants.assertion: Moves reported in the PV are legal when replayed from the root under the engine's own rules.
invariants.why: This validates search output against the rule layer.

invariants.name: tt_move_legal_in_position
invariants.assertion: A transposition-table move retrieved for a position is legal or at least pseudo-legal under the current state policy.
invariants.why: Illegal TT moves indicate key collisions or state corruption.

invariants.name: promotion_budget_feasible_per_side
invariants.assertion: The number of extra queens/rooks/bishops/knights on a side is explainable by missing pawns via promotion.
invariants.why: Material configurations can be locally plausible but globally unreachable.

invariants.name: global_promotion_budget_feasible
invariants.assertion: Combined extra material across both sides does not exceed the total number of promotable pawns that must have disappeared.
invariants.why: This is a stronger global promotion sanity check.

invariants.name: pawn_capture_budget_feasible
invariants.assertion: Pawn-file displacement and survivor counts do not require more captures than are available.
invariants.why: Retrograde reasoning often starts with pawn capture budgets.

invariants.name: pawn_origin_feasible
invariants.assertion: Each pawn arrangement is plausibly derivable from home files under capture constraints; obviously impossible origins are flagged.
invariants.why: Many unreachable positions hide in pawn structure, not in piece movement.

invariants.name: bishop_color_complex_feasible
invariants.assertion: Bishop counts and square-color occupancy are plausible under promotion accounting.
invariants.why: Bishop color-complex arguments are a standard retrograde tool.

invariants.name: rook_knight_queen_excess_explained
invariants.assertion: Surplus rooks, knights, or queens imply corresponding promoted pawns and capture history budgets.
invariants.why: This turns raw material counts into a stronger reachability filter.

invariants.name: impossible_checker_geometry_warned
invariants.assertion: Imported positions with checker constellations that cannot arise from any legal last move are rejected or warned.
invariants.why: python-chess exposes impossible-check style statuses for this reason.

invariants.name: imported_position_validity_level_explicit
invariants.assertion: Imported FENs are classified as basic-valid, heuristic-reachability-pass/fail, or trusted-generated; do not collapse these categories.
invariants.why: The research literature distinguishes local validity from true reachability.

invariants.name: reachable_by_construction_flag
invariants.assertion: States produced from the initial position by your own legal move engine are tagged as trusted-by-construction.
invariants.why: This is the cleanest way to avoid re-solving reachability on internal states.

invariants.name: proof_game_hook_optional
invariants.assertion: Provide a hook for an optional proof-game / retrograde module if arbitrary external legal-position guarantees are required.
invariants.why: Reachability is substantially harder than local validation.

invariants.name: clone_equality
invariants.assertion: Cloning a state yields an equivalent state in all semantically relevant fields.
invariants.why: Basic object-copy correctness supports every other test harness.

invariants.name: fen_roundtrip_normalized_equality
invariants.assertion: parse(serialize(state)) == normalize(state) under the declared EP/castling I/O policy.
invariants.why: Serialization roundtrips are a cheap metamorphic test.

invariants.name: vertical_mirror_color_swap_perft
invariants.assertion: After vertical board mirror plus color swap (and corresponding turn/castling/EP remap), perft at depth d is unchanged.
invariants.why: The rule layer should be symmetric under color-swapping mirror transforms when state metadata is transformed consistently.

invariants.name: horizontal_reflection_perft
invariants.assertion: After horizontal reflection (a-file <-> h-file) with castling/EP file remapping, perft at depth d is unchanged.
invariants.why: Orthodox chess rules are file-symmetric when state metadata is transformed consistently.

invariants.name: make_unmake_involution
invariants.assertion: state == unmake(make(state, move)) for every legal move.
invariants.why: This is the canonical state-transition metamorphic relation for engines.

invariants.name: move_order_independence_of_rule_layer
invariants.assertion: Sorted legal move sets are invariant under any internal move ordering changes.
invariants.why: Search may depend on order, but rule correctness must not.
invariants.implementation_notes: Apply to the rule layer. Do not assume evaluation or search scores are identical at all depths.

invariants.name: search_does_not_mutate_state
invariants.assertion: A pure search call leaves the input state unchanged.
invariants.why: This is a higher-level metamorphic invariant around search entry/exit.

invariants.name: color_swap_eval_sign
invariants.assertion: For an evaluation function expressed from one fixed perspective, color-swapping a position should flip the sign under a documented convention.
invariants.why: Useful for evaluation sanity checks, but not a strict rule oracle.
invariants.implementation_notes: Use only for evaluation testing, not for move legality.

invariants.name: tablebase_wdl_matches_oracle
invariants.assertion: On Syzygy-eligible positions, WDL/DTZ results match the exact tablebase oracle.
invariants.why: Tablebases are the strongest exact oracles available for many endings.

invariants.name: reference_engine_legal_moves_match
invariants.assertion: On random reachable positions, legal move sets match a trusted reference implementation such as python-chess or a reference engine wrapper.
invariants.why: Differential testing is one of the highest-value complements to invariants.

invariants.name: reference_engine_terminal_flags_match
invariants.assertion: On random reachable positions, in-check/checkmate/stalemate/EP/castling availability agree with the reference implementation under the same policy.
invariants.why: Terminal-state and history bugs are common and easy to catch this way.

invariants.name: perft_reference_counts_match
invariants.assertion: Perft counts match the standard corpus on the included reference positions and depths.
invariants.why: Perft is the classic debugging oracle for move generation and make/unmake.
